sourcedFrom: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) (2016 (© 2016 ADVANCED ARMAMENT CORP. / © 2016 RA Brands, L.L.C.))
cleanIntro: The Ti-RANT 45-M is a user-serviceable modular pistol silencer: an aluminium baffle stack in a main tube body, a removable front module that turns it from a 7" compact into a 9" full-size can, and AAC's A.S.A.P. piston system (piston, driving spring and piston housing) threaded onto the rear. AAC's own manual takes it fully apart. The piston system comes out after every range visit, and the baffle stack every 750 dry rounds. ⛔ It is only ever worked on off the host. Never use sandpaper, emery cloth or an ultrasonic cleaner on any part, and clean the baffles only with a solvent that is safe on anodized aluminium.

steps.title: Make the HOST firearm safe first: magazine out, empty, on SAFE
steps.action: Keep the host pointed in a safe direction. Remove the magazine, unload the firearm completely and put its safety on "SAFE", following the host's own manual. A silencer never goes on or comes off a gun you have not checked empty.
steps.prose: This book covers the silencer, not the pistol or carbine it is on. The can has no action to clear, and for unloading the host AAC sends you to the host's own owner's manual.
steps.quote: 2. Render the firearm safe by removing the magazine, completely unloading the firearm and engaging the safety to the "SAFE" position. See the firearm's owner's manual for detailed instructions.
steps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Removing your Ti-RANT 45-M from a host firearm, step 2, P.5
steps.warn: Never install or remove a silencer on or from a host firearm that you have not verified to be completely empty and rendered safe.

steps.title: Let it cool to ambient before you touch it
steps.action: Check that the silencer has cooled to ambient temperature, and let it cool if it is hot. If it has to come off hot, wear heat-resistant gloves.
steps.prose: A can that has just been shot is hot enough to burn a bare hand, and a hot one looks no different from a cold one.
steps.quote: 3. Verify the silencer is at ambient temperature. If the silencer is hot, allow it to cool.
steps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Removing your Ti-RANT 45-M from a host firearm, step 3, P.5
steps.warn: Never handle a hot silencer without heat-resistant gloves, as this may lead to skin burns and/or personal injury.

steps.title: Unscrew it off the muzzle: AGAINST the "ON" arrow on the piston
steps.action: Unscrew the silencer from the muzzle threads, turning it the opposite way to the "ON" arrow marked on the A.S.A.P. piston. Every piston is marked with its thread size and pitch and with that arrow, so read the arrow rather than assuming a direction.
steps.prose: Some pistons carry an O-ring next to the threads that grips the muzzle to stop the can working loose, so expect some drag as it comes off.
steps.quote: 4. Carefully unscrew the silencer from the host firearm's muzzle threads in the opposite of the “ON” direction indicated on the piston.
steps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Removing your Ti-RANT 45-M from a host firearm, step 4, P.5
steps.warn: Only perform disassembly, cleaning, and maintenance procedures on silencers that are not mounted to a firearm.

steps.title: Unscrew the piston housing assembly off the main tube body
steps.action: With the can off the gun, unscrew the piston housing assembly, the rear section carrying the piston, from the main tube body and lift it away.
steps.prose: This is the A.S.A.P. system that lets a tilting-barrel pistol cycle with the can on. It collects carbon fastest, which is why AAC wants it apart after every range visit.
steps.quote: 2. Unscrew and remove the piston housing assembly from the main tube body.
steps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Disassembling your Ti-RANT 45-M A.S.A.P. System, step 2, P.8

steps.title: Press the piston shaft FORWARD out of the housing
steps.action: Press on the rear of the piston shaft, the end with the threaded socket, and push it forward out of the piston housing.
steps.prose: The piston leaves through the front of the housing. Pushing on the threaded rear is the only direction it will go.
steps.quote: 3. Press the rear of the piston shaft forward to remove it from the piston housing.
steps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Disassembling your Ti-RANT 45-M A.S.A.P. System, step 3, P.8

steps.title: Take the driving spring out of the housing
steps.action: Remove the driving spring from inside the piston housing. The A.S.A.P. system is now in three pieces: housing, piston and spring.
steps.prose: Keep the spring with the housing. On a fixed-barrel host AAC recommends swapping this spring for its Fixed-Barrel Spacer, to stop the spring fatiguing early.
steps.quote: 4. Remove the driving spring from the piston housing.
steps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Disassembling your Ti-RANT 45-M A.S.A.P. System, step 4, P.8

steps.title: Field strip complete: the A.S.A.P. system is apart
steps.action: The can is off the host and the piston system is out in three pieces. That is the strip AAC asks for after every range visit. The baffle stack only comes out on its own, longer schedule, and that procedure is under DEEP CLEAN.
steps.prose: Water or another artificial environment speeds up fouling, so the piston system is due sooner when you shoot the can wet.
steps.quote: It is recommended that users disassemble and clean the A.S.A.P. System after every range visit, after 500 rounds of regular use, or after 250 rounds of use with an artificial environment, whichever comes first.
steps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Disassembling your Ti-RANT 45-M A.S.A.P. System, P.7

steps.title: Brush the carbon off the piston
steps.action: With a plastic bristle brush and solvent, scrub the outside of the piston until the accumulated carbon is gone. If your piston has an O-ring beside its rear threads, check it, and replace it if it is worn or frayed.
steps.prose: The piston slides in the housing every shot. Carbon left on it adds friction, and friction there is what makes the host malfunction.
steps.quote: 1. Using a plastic bristle brush and solvent, clean the exterior of the piston of any accumulated carbon.
steps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning/maintaining the A.S.A.P. System, step 1, P.8

steps.title: Brush the piston housing inside and out: nothing harsher than ScotchBrite
steps.action: With a plastic bristle brush and solvent, clean the bore and the outside of the piston housing. Stubborn deposits can take a piece of ScotchBrite moistened with solvent, and nothing more aggressive than that.
steps.prose: The piston, the housing and the rear cap are precision sliding surfaces, and scratching them is how this system starts to stick.
steps.aside: NOTE: Stubborn deposits may require the use of a solvent moistened piece of ScotchBrite cloth to remove.
steps.quote: 3. Using a plastic bristle brush and solvent, clean the bore and the exterior of the A.S.A.P. piston housing.
steps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning/maintaining the A.S.A.P. System, step 3, P.9
steps.warn: Do not use sandpaper or emery cloth to clean any part of a Ti-RANT 45-M silencer.

steps.title: Check the O-ring in the bore of the rear cap
steps.action: Look at the O-ring seated in the bore of the rear cap. If it is worn or frayed, replace it. The manual's O-ring guide lists the Viton replacement sizes.
steps.prose: AAC specifies Viton, a high-temperature material, for every O-ring in this can, so a replacement should be Viton too.
steps.quote: 4. Inspect the O-ring located in the bore of the rear cap. The O-ring is shown colored red in Figures 11 and 12. If it is worn or frayed, replace it.
steps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning/maintaining the A.S.A.P. System, step 4, P.9

steps.title: Clean the interface at the rear of the can: index notches and stop-surfaces
steps.action: With a plastic bristle brush and solvent, clean the interface at the rear of the silencer, where the piston housing threads on. Make sure the piston index notches and the piston stop-surfaces at the front end of the interface are free of carbon.
steps.prose: The piston locates on these notches and stops against these surfaces. Carbon built up there changes where it sits.
steps.quote: 6. Using a plastic bristle brush and solvent, clean the interface in the rear of the silencer. See Figure 17. Insure the piston index notches and piston stop-surfaces located on the front end of the interface are free of carbon buildup.
steps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning/maintaining the A.S.A.P. System, step 6, P.10

steps.title: Grease the rear-cap O-ring, and let ALL the solvent go first
steps.action: Put a small amount of white lithium grease or anti-seize compound on the O-ring in the rear cap. Before the A.S.A.P. system goes back together, let every trace of solvent evaporate.
steps.prose: The waiting is part of the job. Solvent left in the piston system should be gone before it goes back on a gun.
steps.quote: 7. Apply a small amount of white lithium grease or antiseize compound to the Oring in the rear cap (shown colored red in Figures 11 and 12).
steps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning/maintaining the A.S.A.P. System, step 7, P.10
steps.warn: All traces of solvent must be allowed to evaporate prior to reassembling the A.S.A.P. System.

deepSteps.title: Full-size? Unscrew the front end cap off the front module first
deepSteps.action: With the can off the host and the A.S.A.P. system out, a can set up full-size has its front end cap on the front module. Grip the front module around its circumference and unscrew the front end cap. In the compact setup the cap threads straight into the main tube body and there is no front module on the can.
deepSteps.prose: AAC sets the baffle stack's schedule apart from the piston's: every 750 dry rounds, or every 250 shot with an artificial environment.
deepSteps.quote: 3. If your silencer is configured as a full sized model, grasp the silencer around the circumference of the front module and unscrew and remove the front end cap.
deepSteps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Baffle stack removal/maintenance, step 3, P.11
deepSteps.warn: Only perform cleaning and maintenance procedures on silencers that are not mounted to a firearm.

deepSteps.title: Unscrew the front module off the main tube
deepSteps.action: Grip the main tube around its circumference and unscrew the front module from it.
deepSteps.prose: The front module carries three baffles of its own. They come out of the module later, separately from the main tube's stack.
deepSteps.quote: 5. Grasp the silencer around the circumference of the main tube and unscrew and remove the front module.
deepSteps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Baffle stack removal/maintenance, step 5, P.11

deepSteps.title: Push the stack out the FRONT with a 5/8" rod
deepSteps.action: Put a 5/8" rod of wood, plastic or steel in from the rear of the can, through to the rear face of the blast baffle. Hold the can tightly in one hand and push the stack out of the front of the tube with the rod. If hand pressure will not move it, tap the end of the rod gently with a hammer to break the carbon's grip.
deepSteps.prose: The stack only leaves through the front. Pushing it from the rear against the blast baffle moves the whole stack together.
deepSteps.aside: If the baffles will not push out with hand pressure, gently tap the end of the rod with a hammer to break the baffles loose from any accumulated carbon.
deepSteps.quote: 6. Insert a 5/8" rod of wood, plastic, or steel from the rear of the silencer, through the piston housing, and up against the rear face of the blast baffle.
deepSteps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Baffle stack removal/maintenance, step 6, P.11

deepSteps.title: Take the three baffles out of the front module
deepSteps.action: Remove the three baffles from the front module. Note which is which as they come out. The transition baffle has an angled rear face and no tabs, and they go back in a set order.
deepSteps.prose: The two stacks are separate. The main tube holds the blast baffle, four black baffles and a grey front baffle, and the front module holds three more.
deepSteps.quote: 7. Remove the three baffles from the front module.
deepSteps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Baffle stack removal/maintenance, step 7, P.11

deepSteps.title: Brush the baffles: aluminium-safe solvent only
deepSteps.action: Clean the fouling off every baffle with a plastic bristle brush and solvent. Use only a solvent that does not harm anodized aluminium, such as acetone, paint thinner or lacquer thinner. Work somewhere well ventilated, away from open flame, wearing eye protection and solvent-resistant gloves.
deepSteps.prose: The baffles are anodized aluminium, and a solvent that attacks aluminium weakens them without any visible sign.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Clean accumulated fouling from the baffles using a plastic bristle brush and solvent.
deepSteps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning your baffle stack, tube, and front module, step 1, P.12
deepSteps.warn: When cleaning the baffles in a Ti-RANT 45-M silencer, only use a solvent that is not harmful to anodized aluminum, such as acetone, paint thinner, or lacquer thinner.

deepSteps.title: Swab the front end cap's recess and check its O-ring
deepSteps.action: Clean the recess inside the front end cap with a cotton swab. Then check the O-ring on the outside of the cap, and replace it if it looks worn or frayed.
deepSteps.prose: The cap carries its own O-ring. The manual's O-ring guide gives its Viton size.
deepSteps.quote: 2. Use a cotton swab to clean the recess on the inside of the front end cap. See Figure 22. 3. Inspect the O-ring on the outside of the front end cap (shown as red in Figure 22). Replace the O-ring if it appears worn or frayed.
deepSteps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning your baffle stack, tube, and front module, steps 2–3, P.12

deepSteps.title: Scrub inside the main tube body and the front module: no ultrasonic
deepSteps.action: Scrub the inside of the main tube body, then the inside of the front module, with a plastic bristle brush and solvent. Do not put any part of this can in an ultrasonic cleaner.
deepSteps.prose: AAC rules out ultrasonic cleaning because it can damage the aluminium parts.
deepSteps.quote: 4. Scrub the inside of the main tube body using a plastic bristle brush and solvent. See Figure 23. 5. Scrub the inside of the front module using a plastic bristle brush and solvent.
deepSteps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning your baffle stack, tube, and front module, steps 4–5, P.12
deepSteps.warn: Do not clean any part of a Ti-RANT 45-M silencer using an ultrasonic cleaner.

deepSteps.title: Check the front module's O-ring
deepSteps.action: Check the O-ring on the outside of the front module, and replace it if it looks worn or frayed.
deepSteps.prose: The front module and the front end cap use the same size of O-ring.
deepSteps.quote: 6. Inspect the O-ring on the outside of the front module (shown as red in Figure 24). Replace the O-ring if it appears worn or frayed.
deepSteps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning your baffle stack, tube, and front module, step 6, P.13

deepSteps.title: Grease the threads, and let ALL the solvent evaporate before reassembly
deepSteps.action: Coat the outside threads of the front end cap and the front module, and the piston housing interface threads on the outside rear of the tube, with anti-seize compound or white lithium grease. Let every trace of solvent evaporate before anything goes back together.
deepSteps.prose: Greased threads come apart cleanly next time. The baffle order for reassembly is on the reassembly list, and AAC warns against using a can whose core is assembled wrong.
deepSteps.quote: 7. Lubricate the threads on the exterior of the front end cap, front module, and the piston housing interface threads on the exterior rear of the tube with anti-seize compound or white lithium grease.
deepSteps.cite: TM-Ti-RANT® 45-M — TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF SILENCER MODEL Ti-RANT 45-M — 610476 REV-12.16 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning your baffle stack, tube, and front module, step 7, P.13
deepSteps.warn: All traces of solvent must be allowed to evaporate prior to reassembly.

cleaning.name: OFF THE HOST, COLD
tasks: Host firearm: magazine out, fully unloaded, on SAFE
Silencer at ambient temperature, or heat-resistant gloves on
Unscrewed against the "ON" arrow on the piston
Never configured, stripped or cleaned while mounted

cleaning.name: A.S.A.P. PISTON SYSTEM
tasks: Piston exterior brushed free of carbon (plastic bristle brush and solvent)
O-ring beside the piston's rear threads (some pistons) checked; replaced if worn or frayed
Piston housing bore and exterior brushed; ScotchBrite and solvent only for stubborn deposits
Driving spring brushed free of loose material and carbon
Rear-cap bore O-ring checked, replaced if worn or frayed, then a little white lithium grease or anti-seize
Every trace of solvent evaporated before it goes back together

cleaning.name: REAR INTERFACE
tasks: Interface at the rear of the silencer brushed with solvent
Piston index notches and stop-surfaces free of carbon

cleaning.name: LEAVE ALONE
tasks: ⛔ No sandpaper or emery cloth on any part, nothing more aggressive than ScotchBrite
⛔ No ultrasonic cleaner on any part
⛔ No solvent that harms anodized aluminium on the baffles

reassembly: Main-tube stack: one grey front baffle (light grey, no notches on the cone) set cone-side down on a flat, level surface.
First black aluminium baffle on top with its output port 180° opposite the grey baffle's port; its tabs lock into the grey baffle's notches.
Three more black baffles on top, output ports in line with the first black baffle, every tab and notch engaged.
Ported blast baffle on top, its output port in line with the four black baffles.
Tube body slid down over the stack, then the empty front module threaded fully onto the tube body to capture it.
Into the front module: the transition baffle first (angled rear face, no tabs), its output scoop lined up with the scoop of the front baffle in the main tube.
Next the grey baffle with rear tabs and a notched cone, tabbed to the transition baffle with ports aligned; last the second grey front baffle, tabbed and aligned.
Full-size: front end cap installed in the front module. Compact: front module left off and the front end cap threaded fully into the main tube body.
A.S.A.P. system: driving spring into the bore of the piston housing, piston into the housing, and the housing threaded onto the exposed threads at the rear of the interface on the main tube body.
⛔ Never fire it with an incorrectly assembled baffle core.
fncheck: With the host unloaded and on SAFE and the can cold: check the muzzle threads and the threads inside the rear of the A.S.A.P. piston are clean and undamaged. Look through the silencer from the rear to confirm the bullet path is clear. Screw it on by hand in the "ON" direction marked on the piston, tight enough to stay put while firing, and recheck that it is tight (with heat-resistant gloves if it is hot), because keeping it secure is the user's job. ⛔ Fire standard-pressure ammunition only, never +P. Subsonic 300 AAC Blackout goes through it only with AAC's 5/8 x 24 adapter, and supersonic rifle ammunition never. Shot wet, it takes no more than 5cc of water.
